metadata.issueBody:
## Source

google-labs-code/design.md — https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md

## The pattern

`npx @google/design.md diff before.md after.md` detects regressions between two spec versions:

```json
{
  "tokens": {
    "colors": { "added": ["accent"], "removed": [], "modified": ["tertiary"] }
  },
  "regression": false
}
```

Exit code 1 if the "after" file has more errors or warnings than "before" — automated regression gate that runs in CI on every PR touching a spec file.

## The gap in directive

SPECIFICATION.md files and SKILL.md files change across PRs. There is no automated way to detect whether a change is a regression (removes coverage, weakens constraints, breaks references) vs. an improvement. The `deft-pre-pr` skill does a manual Read-Write-Lint-Diff cycle but no semantic diff exists.

## Changes

### `verification/verification.md` — spec regression as a verification tier

When a PR modifies SPECIFICATION.md or a SKILL.md file, the diff should be evaluated for regressions:
- Removed acceptance criteria (coverage regression)
- Removed `!` rules (constraint weakening)
- Broken internal cross-references
- Removed sections without replacement

This is a specific application of the harness audit methodology (issue #445 PR 10).

### `task verify:spec-diff` (future)

Compares SPECIFICATION.md against the base branch and flags regressions — analogous to `@google/design.md diff`. Structured JSON output so `deft-pre-pr` can consume and surface specific findings.

### `task verify:skill-diff` (future)

Same for SKILL.md changes: detect when a skill update removes `requires`, weakens `ensures`, or drops anti-patterns without justification.

## Related

- `verification/verification.md` — target
- `skills/deft-pre-pr/SKILL.md` — consumer of the diff output
- Issue #445 PR 10 — harness audit methodology
- Issue #489 — requires/ensures frontmatter (the structured fields that would be diffed)
